title: compiler_ms decode-cost metering gap: two grammar-authority call sites were unmetered

reproduction.method: python -m scripts.evaluate_model --ship-gates --train-version wf_smoke_v2 --test-dir e938_role_safe_all_targets_v2 --suite smoke --eval-limit 1 against the frozen c1/c2 control checkpoints, decode-timeout raised to 60s so the record finishes instead of being cut off (diagnostic only, never used to claim a passing ship-gate).
reproduction.key_discovery: the c1 control checkpoint's own persisted config declares compiler_decode_mode='off' (it decodes through the legacy LTR/exact_forced_token_id I2-bypass path), while the c2 control/component-plan checkpoints declare compiler_decode_mode='tree' (the compiler-tree greedy path). evaluate_model.py --ship-gates does not force compiler_decode_mode onto a checkpoint unless --compiler-decode-mode is also passed explicitly as a CLI flag (making it a runtime_override_field); otherwise eval_runner.evaluate() restores the checkpoint's own declared value after build_model(). The two prior cycle docs' 'compiler_ms_mean jumped ~5-6x, symmetric across arms' comparison was therefore comparing two DIFFERENT decode mechanisms, not the same search at two seeds.

root_cause: models/grammar.py's exact_forced_token_id() (the legacy non-compiler-tree LTR decode's I2 deterministic-singleton bypass, invoked once per token from _constrained_ltr_repair) calls build_completion_forest() -- the exact same expensive CompletionSession/outgoing()-edge grammar-authority computation the compiler-tree path times as compiler_ms in twotower.py's _compiler_ltr_decode_one/_compiler_ltr_decode_batch -- with zero timed_ms instrumentation anywhere in the call chain. A checkpoint whose own persisted config decodes through this legacy mechanism (compiler_decode_mode='off') can spend effectively all of its real decode wall time inside this one unmetered call while compiler_ms stays 0.0 and the true cost silently lands in unattributed_ms. Separately (defense in depth, smaller effect on this specific case), state.completion_forced_closure() -- called immediately after build_completion_forest() in both _compiler_ltr_decode_one and _compiler_ltr_decode_batch -- performs the same kind of outgoing()-edge walk in a loop that can span the remaining canvas, and was called just outside the timed_ms(compiler_ms) block that wraps only the initial forest build.
not_a_search_algorithm_bug: The completion kernel's own bounds are intact and were not the defect: CompletionSession.terminal_witness caps each top-level candidate to a fixed node_budget (16), LatticeSearchState.backtrack_limit defaults to 8, and check_decode_deadline() is honored throughout every recursive expansion (outgoing/advance/terminal_witness), so a slow decode fails closed with a typed TimeoutError rather than hanging. SemanticState carries a real structural __eq__/memoized __hash__ and OpenUIIncrementalEngine.parser_state_key() is structural (LALR state stack + pending tail), so state interning is not defeated by an identity-based key. The large completion_unique_states/completion_edges_built counts observed (tens of thousands per single ~256-token record) reflect that the grammar-authority computation is a genuinely non-trivial, repeated Lark-based incremental-parse-plus-scope-analysis, invoked once per token (or once per top-level candidate per token) -- not an unbounded or exponential blow-up.

fix.description: Wrap exact_forced_token_id's build_completion_forest call in with timed_ms(get_active_stats(), 'compiler_ms'). Widen the existing with timed_ms(stats, 'compiler_ms') block in _compiler_ltr_decode_one and _compiler_ltr_decode_batch to also cover the immediately-following state.completion_forced_closure(...) call. Both changes are purely additive timing instrumentation -- no decode/generation-output behavior change, no change to which tokens are emitted or which candidates are legal (I2/I6 untouched); only decode_stats attribution changes (compiler_ms measured where it previously wasn't, unattributed_ms shrinks correspondingly).

regression_test.method: monkeypatch build_completion_forest to delay by 50ms while still returning the real result, call exact_forced_token_id under an active DecodeStats, assert stats.compiler_ms captures at least 90% of the delay

conclusion: This is a genuine, now-fixed decode-cost METERING defect in the canonical model_build/twotower decode-stats instrumentation, not evidence of a runaway or exponential compiler-tree search. It directly undermines the specific evidence chain the c5 and gd6j83-c2 docs used ('compiler_ms_mean jumped ~5-6x symmetrically'): that comparison silently pitted a fully-metered decode (compiler_decode_mode=tree) against an almost-entirely-unmetered one (compiler_decode_mode=off), because those two checkpoints/cycles happened to decode through different mechanisms and evaluate_model.py --ship-gates does not force one uniformly without an explicit --compiler-decode-mode flag. Once metered identically, the seed-100001 control's real per-record grammar-authority cost (~38s in this single-record reproduction) is comparable to or larger than seed-100002's (~15-23s/record) -- the two are not obviously different regimes once measured on the same basis. This finding neither confirms nor rules out that the gd6j83-c2 dual-arm timeout itself would reproduce identically under corrected metering; that determination is left to the queued retry_measurement replay per the loop's existing rule (never auto-retire a symmetric dual-arm timeout; require repair first, which this is).
next_steps: retry_measurement on the identical frozen c2 arm (already queued by the loop) now that compiler_ms/unattributed_ms correctly reflect both decode mechanisms

when comparing compiler_ms_mean across cycles/arms going forward, also check each arm's evaluation_policy.compiler_decode_mode -- a symmetric comparison requires both arms to be decoding through the same mechanism, which is not guaranteed by --ship-gates alone

consider (separate, not attempted here) whether evaluate_model.py --ship-gates should warn or fail when a checkpoint's own persisted compiler_decode_mode disagrees with the STRICT_COMPILER_TREE_POLICY_ID it claims to apply, since this silent divergence is what made the metering gap invisible for two prior investigation sessions
